prompt: Gitea runs with --network kind. Which address does a pod inside the cluster use to reach it?

choices.why: That is your machine's loopback, which a pod does not share.

choices.text: http://localhost:3000
choices.why: Inside a pod, localhost is the pod itself.

choices.text: http://gitea:3000
choices.why: Right. On the kind network the container's name resolves, from the node and from its pods.

choices.text: http://kind:3000
choices.why: kind is the network's name, not a container on it.

prompt: Why does the lesson send the new token into ~/ana.token with --raw > instead of letting it print?

choices.text: Because a token in a file expires sooner
choices.why: Where a token is stored does not change when it expires.

choices.text: So that git can read it from that exact path on every push
choices.why: Git reads ~/.git-credentials, which the lesson writes from the file afterwards.

choices.text: Because Gitea cannot print tokens
choices.why: It prints it gladly; --raw prints only the token, for exactly this redirection.

choices.text: So it never appears on the screen
choices.why: Right. A token on the screen ends up in scrollback, screenshots and shared terminals.

prompt: Ana's token was made with --scopes write:repository,write:user. What can a program holding it not do?

choices.text: Administer the Gitea server
choices.why: Right. A token carries only the scopes it was given, whatever its owner may do.

choices.text: Create a repository for Ana
choices.why: write:repository covers that.

choices.text: Open a pull request on fleet
choices.why: That is a repository write as well.

choices.text: Push commits to fleet
choices.why: Pushing is writing a repository.

prompt: An autoscaler owns a deployment's replica count, and the manifest in Git says replicas: 2. What happens?

choices.text: The autoscaler wins, because it runs inside the cluster
choices.why: The agent runs inside the cluster too, and reapplies on every pass.

choices.text: Kubernetes refuses the manifest
choices.why: The manifest is valid; the conflict is between two writers.

choices.text: Git wins once and the autoscaler stops
choices.why: The autoscaler keeps acting on load; it does not give up.

choices.text: They fight: the autoscaler raises it, the agent puts it back
choices.why: Right. One owner per field: leave replicas out of Git, or tell the agent to ignore it.

prompt: Which of these stay out of the configuration repository? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The rows of the application's database
choices.why: Right. That is state the application produces.

choices.text: A database password in clear text
choices.why: Right. base64 is not encryption, and history keeps it for ever.

choices.text: The image reference each environment runs
choices.why: That is exactly what the repository decides.

choices.text: The replica count of a deployment no autoscaler touches
choices.why: With no other owner, Git is the right place for it.

prompt: Two directories in fleet both describe the staging Deployment, with different messages. What does the cluster run?

choices.text: The last one applied, flipping each pass
choices.why: Right. Two truths that disagree make the cluster alternate on every pass.

choices.text: The one in the directory that sorts first
choices.why: Applying both means the later one overwrites the earlier one, every pass.

choices.text: Both, as two separate Deployments
choices.why: They name the same object, so there is one Deployment, rewritten twice.

choices.text: Neither, because Git rejects the duplicate
choices.why: Git stores files; it has no idea two of them describe one object.

prompt: Order the steps of moving a commit that was refused on main onto a branch of its own.
trap: The branch has to exist before main moves back, or the commit is left with no name.

prompt: What does dismiss_stale_approvals protect against?

choices.text: Merging a version the reviewer never saw
choices.why: Right. An approval counts for the commits it was given, not for what was pushed after.

choices.text: Two reviewers approving the same pull request
choices.why: Two approvals are allowed, and sometimes required.

choices.text: Approvals from people who left the company
choices.why: Who may approve is a matter of permissions, not of staleness.

choices.text: A review left open for more than a week
choices.why: Time does not dismiss anything; new commits do.

prompt: A direct push to main is refused with: Not allowed to push to ___ branch main.
In a GitOps setup, what part of a pull request answers why a change was made, a year later?

choices.text: The list of files it touches
choices.why: That is what, again, not why.

choices.text: The merge commit's hash
choices.why: A hash identifies a commit; it explains nothing.

choices.text: Its body
choices.why: Right. The diff says what changed; the body is the record of why.

choices.text: The branch name
choices.why: A branch is deleted after the merge, and a name is not a reason.

prompt: Ana is an administrator of Gitea. Why can she not merge her own pull request?

choices.text: Her token lacks the merge scope
choices.why: She merged pull requests later with the same token, once they were approved.

choices.text: Her own approval does not count
choices.why: Right. Gitea refuses an author's approval, and the rule names nobody as exempt.

choices.text: Administrators may never merge anything
choices.why: Administrators can merge once the rule is satisfied.

choices.text: The pull request had a merge conflict
choices.why: mergeable was true; the refusal named the approvals.

prompt: What HTTP status code did Gitea answer when Ana tried to merge without an approval?
What does kubectl diff show that git diff does not?

choices.text: Who approved the change
choices.why: Neither diff knows about approvals.

choices.text: What would change in the live object
choices.why: Right. It sends the manifests as a dry run and compares with what the cluster holds.

choices.text: Whether the image exists in the registry
choices.why: A dry run does not pull images; lesson 2's broken tag passed it.

choices.text: Which lines of the YAML changed
choices.why: That is exactly what git diff already shows.

prompt: Why does the lesson keep kubectl diff for the reviewer and not put it in the CI check?

choices.text: kubectl diff is too slow for a CI system
choices.why: It took a moment here; speed is not the objection.

choices.text: CI systems cannot install kubectl
choices.why: They can; the question is what it would be allowed to reach.

choices.text: It needs the cluster's credentials
choices.why: Right. Handing CI cluster credentials undoes the pull arrangement for the sake of a check.

choices.text: kubectl diff cannot run without a person typing
choices.why: It runs unattended like any command.

prompt: In kubectl diff, the field metadata.___ going up is Kubernetes saying it will start a rollout.
After the merge, which credentials did reconcile.sh use to clone fleet from Gitea?

choices.text: Bruno's, because he approved
choices.why: Approving gives nobody's credentials to the loop.

choices.text: Ana's, from ~/.git-credentials
choices.why: Right. That is why lesson 3's agent gets a read-only token of its own.

choices.text: None: fleet is a public repository
choices.why: It was created private on purpose.

choices.text: The ci user's token
choices.why: validate.sh uses that one, to post statuses.

prompt: What does kubeconform check, as the lesson uses it?

choices.text: That a reviewer approved the change
choices.why: Approvals are Gitea's business.

choices.text: That the images named in the manifests exist
choices.why: It never contacts a registry; the 1.1 tag passed it.

choices.text: Manifests against the schemas
choices.why: Right. With -strict it also refuses fields the schema does not know.

choices.text: That the cluster can schedule the pods
choices.why: Scheduling is the cluster's job and needs the cluster.

prompt: Why does validate.sh post its status with the ci user's token rather than Ana's?

choices.text: Because statuses from administrators are ignored
choices.why: Gitea counts a status by its context, not by who sent it.

choices.text: Because Ana's token cannot post statuses
choices.why: It has write:repository, which would allow it.

choices.text: So a machine's verdict is never mistaken for a person's
choices.why: Right. The status names who reported it, and that should be the check.

choices.text: So that the check can approve the pull request
choices.why: A status is not an approval, and ci never approves.

prompt: The protection rule requires a commit status whose context is called ___.
Pull request 2 had a failing check and no approval. Which did the merge refusal name?

choices.text: Not allowed to push to protected branch main
choices.why: That is the refusal of a direct push, not of a merge.

choices.text: approve your own pull is not allowed
choices.why: That refuses a self-approval.

choices.text: Does not have enough approvals
choices.why: That was true as well, but not the message this refusal printed.

choices.text: Not all required status checks successful
choices.why: Right. It names the first unmet condition it finds, and here that was the check.

prompt: Staging is merged to an image tag that does not exist. Why does curl still get an answer?

choices.text: The loop refused to apply the change
choices.why: It applied it; the deployment reported one up-to-date replica.

choices.text: Old pods stay until new ones are ready
choices.why: Right. A new pod that never becomes ready replaces nothing.

choices.text: Kubernetes ignores images it cannot pull
choices.why: It tries and keeps retrying; the pod sits in ErrImagePull.

choices.text: kubeconform rolled the change back
choices.why: kubeconform checks files and never touches the cluster.

prompt: Why is kubectl rollout undo not the fix here?

choices.text: Gitea's protection rule blocks it
choices.why: The rule protects a branch, not the cluster.

choices.text: rollout undo only works on StatefulSets
choices.why: It works on Deployments; it simply does not last.

choices.text: The loop reapplies main on its next pass
choices.why: Right. The fix has to go where the truth is, which is Git.

choices.text: It needs the image of the bad version
choices.why: Undo goes back to the previous template, which needs nothing new.

prompt: To revert a merge commit, git revert needs to be told which parent is the mainline: git revert ___ 1 HEAD.
What does a force-push back to before the bad merge lose that a revert keeps?

choices.text: The record that 1.1 was merged, failed and was undone
choices.why: Right. History that can be rewritten is not a record.

choices.text: Bruno's account
choices.why: Accounts are not part of a branch's history.

choices.text: The commits that came before the bad merge
choices.why: A force-push to an earlier commit keeps everything before it.

choices.text: The image 1.0 in the registry
choices.why: Git operations do not touch the registry.

prompt: During an incident, why is pausing the agent and editing the cluster by hand ruled out?

choices.text: It is slower than any pull request
choices.why: It is usually faster, which is why it is tempting.

choices.text: The fix is undone on resume
choices.why: Right. Cluster and repository disagree, and nothing tracks it.

choices.text: Kubernetes refuses edits while an agent is paused
choices.why: Kubernetes takes the edit; the danger is what happens after.

choices.text: Pausing an agent deletes the objects it applied
choices.why: Pausing stops it from acting; nothing is deleted.

prompt: Which belong to the break-glass path the lesson describes? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A dedicated account allowed to push to main
choices.why: Right. Not a person's everyday account.

choices.text: A pull request after the fact explaining the change
choices.why: Right. The record is never skipped, only the wait.

choices.text: Turning off the branch protection for the night
choices.why: That is a quietly weakened rule, the thing the path replaces.

choices.text: Credentials kept where reading them is itself an event
choices.why: Right. A sealed envelope, a vault that logs every read.

prompt: Match each refusal to its cause.

pairs.right: The token matched none on the server
The approval was dismissed by a new push
No stored credential for that address

pairs.left: approve your own pull is not allowed

right_distractors: The branch has a merge conflict

prompt: ~/.git-credentials has a line for http://localhost:3000, and the remote is http://127.0.0.1:3000. What does Git do on a push?

choices.text: Uses the stored credential, since both reach Gitea
choices.why: Git matches the credential by the name in the URL, not by where it leads.

choices.text: Rewrites the remote to localhost
choices.why: Git never rewrites a remote on its own.

choices.text: Asks for a username, because the hosts differ
choices.why: Right. To Git they are two servers, and only one has a credential.

choices.text: Pushes anonymously and is refused for being private
choices.why: It asks first, because a credential could be supplied.

prompt: Order the life of pull request 2, from the push to the cluster.
trap: The check runs on every new commit, and Bruno approves after the check, on the version that will be merged.

prompt: A colleague says: we have branch protection, so we can give the CI system cluster-admin to run kubectl diff on every pull request. What is wrong with it?

choices.text: cluster-admin is not enough to run kubectl diff
choices.why: It is more than enough, which is the problem.

choices.text: Every job in CI would again be a step from the cluster's keys
choices.why: Right. The protection guards main; it does nothing for a credential CI holds.

choices.text: kubectl diff cannot compare a branch with the cluster
choices.why: It compares whatever manifests it is given.

choices.text: Branch protection forbids CI from reading the cluster
choices.why: Protection rules govern Git operations, not cluster access.

prompt: How many pull requests did this lesson merge into fleet's main?
Why is fleet created as a private repository?

choices.text: The cluster can only read private ones
choices.why: The agent reads either, with a token.

choices.text: Gitea cannot serve public repositories
choices.why: It serves both.

choices.text: It describes production
choices.why: Right. That is nobody's business outside the team.

choices.text: Private repositories are faster to clone
choices.why: Visibility does not change speed.

prompt: Why is ~/.git-credentials made readable only by you?

choices.text: It speeds up the credential helper
choices.why: Permissions do not change speed.

choices.text: Gitea checks the file's permissions
choices.why: Gitea never sees the file.

choices.text: Git refuses world-readable files
choices.why: Git reads it either way.

choices.text: It holds the token in clear
choices.why: Right. Anyone reading it could push as you.

prompt: A tool renders manifests from templates. What usually goes in Git?

choices.text: The templates and their values
choices.why: Right. The agent renders them; lesson 6 covers the exception.

choices.text: Only the rendered output
choices.why: That is the exception, not the rule.

choices.text: Both, in the same directory
choices.why: Two copies of one truth disagree.

choices.text: Neither; the tool's cache holds them
choices.why: Nothing outside Git is the truth.

prompt: The protection rule blocks direct pushes 'administrators included'. Why include them?

choices.text: Gitea requires it for any rule
choices.why: It is a setting, not a requirement.

choices.text: Administrators cannot open pull requests
choices.why: They can, and must, like everybody.

choices.text: It makes merges faster
choices.why: It makes nothing faster.

choices.text: An exception for admins is a way round the review
choices.why: Right. Nobody's change reaches main unreviewed.

prompt: What does a pull request's body record that the diff cannot?

choices.text: Who pushed the branch
choices.why: The server records that by itself.

choices.text: Why the change was made
choices.why: Right. Lesson 12 reads it back.

choices.text: When the cluster applied it
choices.why: Flux's events record that.

choices.text: Which lines changed
choices.why: The diff shows that.

prompt: When do git diff and kubectl diff stop agreeing?

choices.text: Whenever the branch has two commits
choices.why: The number of commits does not matter.

choices.text: When the live object has drifted
choices.why: Right. Or a default the cluster filled in differs.

choices.text: Only for Secrets
choices.why: Any object can drift.

choices.text: Never; they read the same files
choices.why: kubectl diff reads the live object too.

prompt: What does -strict add to kubeconform's check?

choices.text: It validates the image exists
choices.why: It knows nothing about registries.

choices.text: It contacts the cluster to compare
choices.why: kubeconform never contacts a cluster.

choices.text: It refuses fields the schema does not know
choices.why: Right. A misspelt field becomes an error.

choices.text: It requires every optional field
choices.why: Optional fields stay optional.

prompt: replicas: three failed the check. Why?

choices.text: The schema wants an integer
choices.why: Right. A word is a string.

choices.text: replicas cannot be set in staging
choices.why: It can, and is.

choices.text: Three replicas is above the limit
choices.why: There is no such limit.

choices.text: The field name was misspelt
choices.why: The name was right; the value was wrong.

prompt: bulletin:1.1 passed the check and broke the rollout. Why did the check pass?

choices.text: kubeconform only checks Services
choices.why: It checks every object.

choices.text: Bruno approved before it ran
choices.why: Approval does not change the check.

choices.text: The check was skipped
choices.why: It ran and posted success.

choices.text: A tag that does not exist is a valid string
choices.why: Right. kubeconform checks shapes, not registries.

prompt: Why does the revert go through the check and the review?

choices.text: It is a change like any other
choices.why: Right. The flow does not care which direction a change goes.

choices.text: Reverts need two approvals
choices.why: One is enough, as for any change.

choices.text: The loop only applies reviewed reverts
choices.why: The loop applies whatever main says.

choices.text: Gitea cannot merge reverts directly
choices.why: It could; the rule is what stops it.

prompt: What makes the normal path fast enough for an incident? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Checks that take seconds
choices.why: Right. A slow check is skipped when it matters.

choices.text: Pausing the agent during the fix
choices.why: That leaves the cluster and Git disagreeing.

choices.text: Somebody available to approve
choices.why: Right. A rota, or an agreement.

choices.text: Small diffs
choices.why: Right. They are reviewed in seconds.

prompt: Gitea answers 401 with 'invalid username, password or token'. What is the first thing to check?

choices.text: That the token file has the token you made
choices.why: Right. wc -c should say 41.

choices.text: That the repository is private
choices.why: Visibility gives 404, not 401.

choices.text: That the cluster is running
choices.why: The cluster is not involved.

choices.text: That Bruno approved
choices.why: Approval has nothing to do with authentication.
